name: Function
FactorsThrough
result.type: {α : Sort u_1} → {β : Sort u_2} → {γ : Sort u_3} → (α → γ) → (α → β) → Prop
result.value:
:=
  ∀ ⦃a b⦄, f a = f b → g a = g b
result.informal_name: Function g factors through function f
result.informal_description: The proposition that for all $a, b$, if $f(a) = f(b)$ then $g(a) = g(b)$. This means the function $g$ respects the equivalence relation induced by $f$.

name: Function
factorsThrough_iff
result.signature: (g : α → γ) [Nonempty γ] : g.FactorsThrough f ↔ ∃ (e : β → γ), g = e ∘ f
result.type:
∀ {α : Sort u_1} {β : Sort u_2} {γ : Sort u_3} {f : α → β} (g : α → γ) [Nonempty γ],
  Function.FactorsThrough g f ↔ ∃ e, g = e ∘ f
result.value:
:=
  ⟨fun hf =>
    ⟨extend f g (const β (Classical.arbitrary γ)), funext (fun x => by simp only [comp_apply, hf.extend_apply])⟩,
    fun h _ _ hf => by rw [Classical.choose_spec h, comp_apply, comp_apply, hf]⟩
result.informal_name: Factorization Through a Function iff Existence of Intermediate Function
result.informal_description: For a function $g : \alpha \to \gamma$ with $\gamma$ non-empty, the function $g$ factors through $f$ (i.e., whenever $f(a) = f(b)$, then $g(a) = g(b)$) if and only if there exists a function $e : \beta \to \gamma$ such that $g = e \circ f$.

name: Function
FactorsThrough
extend_apply
result.signature: {g : α → γ} (hf : g.FactorsThrough f) (e' : β → γ) (a : α) : extend f g e' (f a) = g a
result.type:
∀ {α : Sort u_1} {β : Sort u_2} {γ : Sort u_3} {f : α → β} {g : α → γ},
  Function.FactorsThrough g f → ∀ (e' : β → γ) (a : α), Function.extend f g e' (f a) = g a
result.value:
:= by
  classical
  simp only [extend_def, dif_pos, exists_apply_eq_apply]
  exact hf (Classical.choose_spec (exists_apply_eq_apply f a))
result.informal_name: Extended Function Agrees with Original on Image of f
result.informal_description: If $g$ factors through $f$ (i.e., $f(a) = f(b)$ implies $g(a) = g(b)$), then for any fallback function $e' : \beta \to \gamma$, the extended function satisfies $\text{extend}(f, g, e')(f(a)) = g(a)$ for all $a \in \alpha$.

name: CategoryTheory
Subobject
factorThru
congr_simp
result.signature:
∀ {C : Type u₁} [inst : CategoryTheory.Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {X Y : C} (P : CategoryTheory.Subobject Y) (f f_1 : X ⟶ Y)
  (e_f : f = f_1) (h : P.Factors f), P.factorThru f h = P.factorThru f_1 ⋯
result.type:
∀ {C : Type u₁} [inst : CategoryTheory.Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {X Y : C} (P : CategoryTheory.Subobject Y) (f f_1 : X ⟶ Y)
  (e_f : f = f_1) (h : P.Factors f), P.factorThru f h = P.factorThru f_1 ⋯
result.informal_description: In a category $\mathcal{C}$, for objects $X$ and $Y$, a subobject $P$ of $Y$, and a morphism $f : X \to Y$ that factors through $P$ (i.e., there exists a morphism $g : X \to \text{dom}(P)$ such that $g \circ \text{mono}_P = f$), the function `factorThru` returns the morphism $g$ witnessing this factorization. The output is constructed by selecting a representative from the proof that such a factorization exists.

name: Function
FactorsThrough
comp_left
result.signature: {α β γ δ : Sort*} {f : α → β} {g : α → γ} (h : FactorsThrough g f) (g' : γ → δ) : FactorsThrough (g' ∘ g) f
result.type:
∀ {α : Sort u_1} {β : Sort u_2} {γ : Sort u_3} {δ : Sort u_4} {f : α → β} {g : α → γ},
  Function.FactorsThrough g f → ∀ (g' : γ → δ), Function.FactorsThrough (g' ∘ g) f
result.informal_name: Composition on the Left Preserves Factorization Through
result.informal_description: If a function $g : \alpha \to \gamma$ factors through $f : \alpha \to \beta$ (i.e., $f(a) = f(b)$ implies $g(a) = g(b)$), then composing $g$ with any function $g' : \gamma \to \delta$ preserves this property: the composition $g' \circ g$ also factors through $f$.

name: Function
FactorsThrough
extend_comp
result.signature: {g : α → γ} (e' : β → γ) (hf : FactorsThrough g f) : extend f g e' ∘ f = g
result.type:
∀ {α : Sort u_1} {β : Sort u_2} {γ : Sort u_3} {f : α → β} {g : α → γ} (e' : β → γ),
  Function.FactorsThrough g f → Function.extend f g e' ∘ f = g
result.value:
:=
  funext fun a => hf.extend_apply e' a
result.informal_name: Composition of Extended Function with Original Function Recovers the Original Function
result.informal_description: If $g : \alpha \to \gamma$ factors through $f : \alpha \to \beta$ (i.e., $f(a) = f(b)$ implies $g(a) = g(b)$), then composing the extended function $\text{extend}(f, g, e') : \beta \to \gamma$ with $f$ yields the original function $g$. Formally, $\text{extend}(f, g, e') \circ f = g$.

name: Function
Fiber
map_eq_image
result.signature: (f : Y → Z) (a : Fiber f) (x : a.1) : f x = a.image
result.type: ∀ {Y : Type u_2} {Z : Type u_3} (f : Y → Z) (a : Function.Fiber f) (x : ↑↑a), f ↑x = Function.Fiber.image f a
result.value:
:= by
  have := a.2.choose_spec
  rw [← Set.mem_singleton_iff, ← Set.mem_preimage]
  convert x.prop
result.informal_name: Function maps fiber elements to their image
result.informal_description: For any function $ f : Y 	o Z $, if $ a $ is a fiber of $ f $ and $ x $ is an element of $ a $, then $ f(x) $ equals the image of the fiber $ a $.

name: Function
FactorsThrough
rfl
result.signature: {α β : Sort*} {f : α → β} : FactorsThrough f f
result.type: ∀ {α : Sort u_1} {β : Sort u_2} {f : α → β}, Function.FactorsThrough f f
result.informal_name: Reflexivity of Function Factorization Through Itself
result.informal_description: For any function $ f : \alpha \to \beta $, the function $ f $ factors through itself. This means that whenever $ f(a) = f(b) $, it follows that $ f(a) = f(b) $, which is trivially true by reflexivity.

name: Measurable
factorsThrough
result.signature: [MeasurableSpace Z] [MeasurableSingletonClass Z] (hg : Measurable[mY.comap f] g) : g.FactorsThrough f
result.type:
∀ {X : Type u_1} {Y : Type u_2} {Z : Type u_3} [mY : MeasurableSpace Y] {f : X → Y} {g : X → Z}
  [inst : MeasurableSpace Z] [MeasurableSingletonClass Z], Measurable g → Function.FactorsThrough g f
result.value:
:= by
  refine fun x₁ x₂ h ↦ eq_of_mem_singleton ?_
  obtain ⟨s, -, hs⟩ := hg (measurableSet_singleton (g x₂))
  rw [← mem_preimage, ← hs, mem_preimage, h, ← mem_preimage, hs, mem_preimage, mem_singleton_iff]
result.informal_name: Measurable Function Factors Through Another Function Under Comap Condition
result.informal_description: Given a measurable space on $ Z $ and the property that all singletons in $ Z $ are measurable, if a function $ g : Y 	o Z $ is measurable with respect to the preimage $\sigma$-algebra induced by a function $ f : X 	o Y $, then $ g $ factors through $ f $. This means that whenever $ f(a) = f(b) $, it follows that $ g(a) = g(b) $.
